task: Migrate the canonical Shoperation Living Roadmap to the accepted v2 maturity sequence and prerequisite graph without changing commerce runtime behavior.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: The change moves a canonical planning authority and its consumers, so it requires explicit dependency invariants, failure-path review and exact-reference checks, but it does not modify runtime commerce behavior or production data.

acceptanceCriteria: Exactly one canonical Living Roadmap authority remains and all known consumers read the v2 file.
The nine accepted maturity stages form a valid dependency chain with no missing references, cycles or reverse-order dependencies.
Historical evidence-backed done and operational states remain represented without being misused as proof of later maturity gates.
Builder and Template Factory are separate registry capabilities and the Factory cannot precede Builder adversarial acceptance.
No commerce runtime, template implementation or SPORT HUB production work is introduced by this transaction.
invariants: Higher-layer maturity cannot prove a lower-layer maturity gate.
Core capability completion and adversarial proof occur before Unified Product Experience and Builder completion.
Builder adversarial acceptance occurs before Factory revalidation and 42-template production.
Final Market Ready certification runs after Surface Reduction on the reduced production candidate.
The Evidence Ledger remains proof-only and cannot override roadmap, capability or domain truth.

failureModes: A consumer keeps importing the retired v1 roadmap and silently diverges from the new canonical order.
A new maturity node references a missing roadmap item or unknown capability and architecture health still reports PASS.
Historical implementation labels are interpreted as proof that a new maturity gate is complete.
Template Factory or portfolio production becomes schedulable before the manual Builder is complete and adversarially proven.
Market Ready certification is treated as a place to add missing core functionality instead of a final closure gate.
edgeCases: The v1 roadmap is deleted while one test or script still references its path.
A new capability registry entry points to a roadmap item that was renamed during migration.
Two roadmap items share the same order but have no dependency relation.
Post-launch and parked items remain visible without becoming accidental Market Ready dependencies.

alternatives.summary: Replace the v1 roadmap authority with one canonical v2 maturity graph and migrate every known consumer to it.
alternatives.reason: This preserves a single machine-readable roadmap authority while making the accepted maturity order explicit and testable.

alternatives.summary: Keep the existing v1 file and only annotate the old feature order with prose about the new maturity sequence.
alternatives.reason: The old machine-readable order would remain authoritative and could continue driving Builder, Factory and Market Ready work in the wrong sequence.

challenge.scenario: A higher-layer template or Builder proof is green while a lower-layer Core capability is still partial.
challenge.finding: Without explicit maturity dependencies the system could overclaim readiness from unrelated higher-layer evidence.
challenge.resolution: The v2 backbone requires each later maturity gate to depend on the preceding gate and records that higher-layer proof cannot close lower-layer gaps.

challenge.scenario: The v1 roadmap file is retired but a quality script or test still imports the old path.
challenge.finding: The repository would have a hidden stale consumer or fail after merge despite a logically correct v2 graph.
challenge.resolution: All discovered consumers are migrated to v2 and architecture tests assert the v2 contract and maturity chain.

challenge.scenario: Builder and Template Factory stay represented as one capability after the maturity order separates them.
challenge.finding: Capability evidence could falsely allow Factory proof to stand in for Builder maturity or vice versa.
challenge.resolution: The capability registry splits Visual Builder from Template Production System / Factory while retaining the same DOMAIN-BUILDER owner authority.

specialistReviews.finding: The accepted roadmap is a maturity graph, not a linear feature backlog, and the canonical authority must encode dependency gates directly.
specialistReviews.resolution: Use nine explicit maturity nodes and keep feature capabilities beneath the Core and Builder gates instead of allowing order numbers alone to imply readiness.

specialistReviews.finding: Deleting the v1 authority can create stale-path failures or hidden parallel truth if even one consumer is missed.
specialistReviews.resolution: Migrate every discovered consumer, delete v1 on the same transaction, and run full knowledge-infrastructure Known Failure replay plus quality tests.

proofPlan: Run the canonical development guards against the exact PR base and head using this active-plan transaction identity.
Run Architecture Health and quality tests to prove all roadmap references, capability references and maturity dependencies are coherent.
Run TypeScript and production build to detect stale imports of the retired v1 roadmap path.
Verify the v2 graph has no missing dependency, cycle or topological-order violation and preserves evidence-backed historical done states.
Require Completion Truth to remain NOT DONE unless exact-head quality, typecheck and production-build evidence satisfy the declared requirements.

requirements.requirement: The canonical quality-system roadmap authority is Living Roadmap v2, the v1 authority is retired, and the migrated canonical roadmap consumers no longer reference the v1 path.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: A second canonical roadmap or stale v1 consumer must not remain active.

requirements.requirement: The accepted nine-stage maturity backbone and its critical dependencies are machine-validated without missing references or reverse sequencing.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Builder, Factory, templates or Market Ready must not bypass their required lower-layer maturity gate.

requirements.requirement: The roadmap migration changes planning and quality authority only and does not introduce commerce, Builder or template runtime feature behavior.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: The transaction must not silently expand into commerce runtime or template implementation work.

notes: Canonical roadmap reconciliation and authority migration only. This transaction records accepted PO decisions, replaces the old feature-order roadmap with the v2 maturity graph, retires the v1 authority, splits Builder from Template Factory in the capability registry, and updates quality consumers/tests. No storefront, commerce runtime, Builder implementation or template production is in scope.
